ANSWER: YES
MISSING_TERMS:
- Full list of Lenders party to Amendment No. 5 (as enumerated in the source): JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. (Administrative Agent and Lender); Citibank, N.A.; Bank of America, N.A.; Wells Fargo Bank, NA; Deutsche Bank AG New York Branch; Goldman Sachs Bank USA; Mizuho Bank, Ltd.; BNP Paribas; Royal Bank of Canada; U.S. Bank National Association; Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A.; MUFG Bank, Ltd.; Societe Generale; Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation; The Toronto-Dominion Bank, New York Branch; Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited, New York Branch; The Bank of New York Mellon; The Northern Trust Company; Truist Bank.
- Amendment No. 5 Effective Date mechanics (condition to effectiveness: becomes effective upon Administrative Agent’s receipt of executed counterparts from Paramount and Required Lenders; Agent to notify parties of the Effective Date).
- Detailed Consolidated EBITDA definition elements:
  - Exclusion of amortization related to programming rights, prepublication costs, videocassettes and DVDs.
  - Specific treatment of gains/losses on asset sales, including exceptions for ordinary-course inventory sales and de minimis thresholds ($10,000,000 individually and $50,000,000 aggregate).
  - Enumerated non-cash addbacks: provisions for losses/valuation allowances; restructuring/litigation/environmental reserves; pension settlement charges; ASC 718 stock-based compensation; impairment charges.
  - Inclusion of expenses incurred in connection with acquisitions, Dispositions or merger transactions in accordance with ASC 805.
  - Cash items included under clause (d) categories (restructuring/business optimization, litigation and environmental reserves, and losses on Disposition of businesses) subject to the 15% cap (already noted generally but missing the specific categories).
- Two-period formulation of the Consolidated Total Leverage Ratio (full Unrestricted Cash netting for fiscal quarters on or after March 31, 2022 and on or prior to June 30, 2024; $3,000,000,000 Unrestricted Cash cap thereafter).
